@graph.d3f:definition: The adversary re-sends previously valid commands or procedures to cause the spacecraft to transmit data again, then captures the resulting downlink. Typical targets are recorder playbacks, payload product dumps, housekeeping snapshots, or file directory listings. By aligning replays with geometry (e.g., when the satellite is in view of actor-controlled apertures) and with acceptance conditions (counters, timetags, mode), the attacker induces legitimate transmissions that appear routine to operators. Variants include selectively replaying index ranges to fetch only high-value intervals, reissuing subscription/telemetry-rate changes to increase data volume, or queueing playbacks that fire during later passes when interception is feasible.
@graph.rdfs:label: Replay - SPARTA
